title: DBML sidecar anchor manifest
description: Schema for analysis/views/dbml/anchor_manifest.json produced in orchestrated mode. Required by ART-VAL-001-07 (anchor manifest required) per skills/bsa-orchestrator/references/sidecar-integration.md. Consumed by the orchestrator's sidecar validator, by future downstream regression tooling, and by the v1.2.6 sidecar e2e fixture (extended in v1.2.11 to cover DBML). Extends the common base at governance/schemas/sidecar_anchor_manifest.base.schema.json — the base requires the 5 top-level fields (manifest_version / generated_at / sidecar / canon_policy_version / view_files) and the per-view-file path + anchor_map array; this per-sidecar schema pins the DBML-specific shape (sidecar literal, path extension, view-element-kind enum).

bounded_context.description: Short identifier for the DB / service / bounded context this .dbml file models. Helps operators distinguish multi-context schemas when one workspace ships several .dbml files. Intentionally free-form snake_case (no coupled enum) so per-engagement conventions drive the vocabulary.

view_element_id.description: Per the DBML sidecar's integration-contract convention: tables use bare name (e.g., `users`); columns use `<table>.<column>` (e.g., `users.id`); refs use `ref_<from_table>_<from_col>_to_<to_table>_<to_col>`; enums and table groups use bare name. Multi-occurrence same-(from,to) refs get `__N` suffix starting at `__2`.

view_element_kind.description: DBML element kind. Enum is intentionally small (5 kinds) — DBML's grammar is far smaller than C4-PlantUML's or BPMN 2.0's. Cardinality discriminators (short arrow / long arrow / dash for one-to-one vs many-to-one) collapse to the single `Ref` kind at the bridge layer; cardinality rides in the optional `notes` field when operators want to track it.

notes.description: Optional free-text annotation. Common content: cardinality hints for Ref-kind anchors, PK/FK role for Column-kind, which bounded context the Table belongs to when the .dbml is part of a multi-file schema pack.
